mainTopic: The status of a blemished בכור: who may eat it (a זר, a גוי, נדות) and whether it may be skinned from the feet
overview: This amud discusses who may eat a blemished בכור and how it must be treated. First, בית הלל answer בית שמאי: the comparison to holy meat applies only to a תם. For a בעל מום the תורה says even a טמא may eat it, and from there they build a קל וחומר that a זר may eat it too. The גמרא tries to refute the קל וחומר from עבודת ציבור, and בית הלל answer that the argument is about eating, where a זר is stronger. Next, רבי עקיבא allows even a גוי, learning it from 'כצבי וכאיל'. The other opinion explains that each of the three appearances of צבי ואיל teaches something else. A second ברייתא records that בית שמאי forbid feeding a blemished בכור to נדות and בית הלל permit it, with each side bringing proofs, including the case of a פסח brought in טומאה. Finally, a ברייתא forbids skinning from the feet on יום טוב, for a בכור, and for פסולי המוקדשין. רב חסדא attributes the בכור ruling to בית שמאי and the פסולי המוקדשין ruling to רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון, explaining that a בכור's holiness is from the womb.

steps.title: בית הלל limit בית שמאי's source to an unblemished בכור
steps.stepSummary: בית הלל answer that בית שמאי's proof applies only to an unblemished בכור. For a blemished one, the תורה says even a טמא may eat it.
steps.simpleTranslation: And בית הלל would answer: that source only applies to an unblemished animal. But about a blemished one it is written: 'The impure and the pure may eat it alike.'
steps.whatsHappening: בית הלל respond to בית שמאי's proof that only a כהן may eat a בכור. They say that proof is about a תם (an unblemished animal), and they bring a different פסוק for a בעל מום.
steps.deeperAnalysis: בית שמאי compared the בכור to parts of offerings that only כהנים eat. בית הלל agree with that comparison, but only for an unblemished בכור that goes on the מזבח. For a blemished בכור, the פסוק 'הטמא והטהור יחדיו' shows that the rules are much more relaxed. This פסוק becomes the base for the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: This rule applies only to... (a limiting phrase)
An unblemished animal, fit for the altar
An animal with a blemish, unfit for the altar
A ritually impure person
Together, alike

phrases.english: And Beit Hillel would respond: this applies only to an unblemished one,
phrases.notes: בית הלל answer בית שמאי's earlier proof, which is not part of this passage.

phrases.english: but concerning a blemished one it is written:
"the impure and the pure may eat it alike,"
phrases.notes: Based on דברים 12:22 and 15:22, which speak about a blemished בכור.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers בית שמאי's derivation, which came earlier in the ברייתא on the previous amud.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the source to a different case (a תם, not a בעל מום)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: בית שמאי's comparison would restrict every בכור to כהנים.
steps.terutzMaskana: The restriction applies only to an unblemished בכור. A blemished בכור follows the פסוק that allows even a טמא to eat it.

steps.title: A קל וחומר from an impure כהן to a non-כהן
steps.stepSummary: If a טמא כהן, who cannot eat קדשים קלים, may still eat a blemished בכור, then a זר, who can eat קדשים קלים, should certainly be allowed to eat it.
steps.simpleTranslation: A ritually impure person cannot eat offerings of lesser holiness, yet he may eat the firstborn. So a non-כהן, who may eat offerings of lesser holiness, should surely be allowed to eat the firstborn.
steps.whatsHappening: בית הלל build a קל וחומר from the פסוק to prove that a זר may eat a blemished בכור.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The 'weaker' case is the טמא, who is barred even from קדשים קלים, and the פסוק still lets him eat the בכור. The 'stronger' case is the זר, who is allowed to eat קדשים קלים. If the weaker one is allowed, the stronger one should be allowed too.

keyTerms.meaning: An argument from a weaker case to a stronger case
Offerings of lesser holiness (such as a שלמים)
A non-כהן
Is it not logical? (the closing formula of a קל וחומר)
A firstborn male animal, which belongs to the כהן

steps.confusionAlert: The 'טמא' here is an impure כהן. A non-כהן is not the subject of this side of the comparison. The argument compares an impure כהן with a pure non-כהן.

phrases.aramaic: וּמָה טָמֵא שֶׁאֵינוֹ אוֹכֵל בְּקָדָשִׁים קַלִּים
phrases.english: And if an impure person, who may not eat offerings of lesser sanctity,
may eat of the firstborn,
then a non-priest, who may eat offerings of lesser sanctity,
is it not logical that he may eat of the firstborn?

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמָה טָמֵא שֶׁאֵינוֹ אוֹכֵל בְּקָדָשִׁים קַלִּים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the פסוק from step 1 as the base of a קל וחומר.
steps.raayaObject: That a זר may eat a blemished בכור
steps.raayaSupportSource: A קל וחומר built on the פסוק 'הטמא והטהור יחדיו יאכלנו'

steps.title: Refuting the קל וחומר: an impure כהן is allowed in public service
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the קל וחומר. A טמא has a special leniency that a זר never has: he may do עבודת ציבור when needed.
steps.simpleTranslation: This can be refuted. What is special about an impure person? His general prohibition was permitted in the case of public service.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks בית הלל's קל וחומר by showing that the 'weaker' case, the טמא, is actually stronger in a different way.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A קל וחומר only works if the starting case is weaker in every relevant way. A טמא כהן may perform communal offerings when there are no pure כהנים (טומאה הותרה בציבור), but a זר may never do any עבודה. So the טמא has an advantage the זר lacks, and the קל וחומר seems to fall apart.

keyTerms.meaning: It can be refuted (an attack on a קל וחומר)
What about X? It has a special feature... (the standard refutation formula)
Was permitted out of its general prohibition
Communal sacrificial service

phrases.english: It can be refuted:
what about an impure person? He has the feature that he was permitted out of his general prohibition
for communal service!
phrases.notes: When there are no pure כהנים, impure כהנים may bring communal offerings. A non-כהן can never serve.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the קל וחומר of step 2.
steps.kashyaTarget: בית הלל's קל וחומר from טמא to זר
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The טמא is not weaker in every way. He has a leniency in עבודת ציבור that a זר never has, so you cannot learn the זר from him.

steps.title: בית הלל answer that the argument is about eating, not service
steps.stepSummary: בית הלל answer that the קל וחומר is about eating. When it comes to eating, a זר is better off than a טמא, so the refutation does not apply.
steps.simpleTranslation: And בית הלל would answer: are we talking about service? We are talking about eating, and when it comes to eating, a non-כהן has the advantage.
steps.whatsHappening: בית הלל reject the refutation by saying it comes from the wrong area of law.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The refutation pointed to a leniency in עבודה (service). The קל וחומר is about אכילה (eating), and there the זר clearly has the advantage, because he eats קדשים קלים and the טמא does not. A leniency from a different area does not break an argument about eating, so the קל וחומר stands.

keyTerms.meaning: Is that to say...? (introduces a rhetorical rejection)
Sacrificial service
Eating
Is superior, has the advantage

steps.whatToRemember: בית הלל's קל וחומר survives because it is about eating. In eating, a זר is stronger than a טמא, so a זר may eat a blemished בכור.

phrases.english: And Beit Hillel: is it said with regard to service?
We are speaking with regard to eating,
and the eating of a non-priest is superior.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the refutation of step 3 and saves the קל וחומר of step 2.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Separating the areas of law (eating versus service)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The טמא's leniency in עבודת ציבור makes him stronger than a זר, so the קל וחומר fails.
steps.terutzMaskana: The קל וחומר is only about eating, and in eating the זר is stronger. The argument holds.

steps.title: Asking for רבי עקיבא's source for allowing even a גוי
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes רבי עקיבא's view from the ברייתא that even a גוי may eat a blemished בכור, and asks for his source.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי עקיבא permits it, even to a non-Jew. What is רבי עקיבא's reason?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to the next opinion in the ברייתא, quotes it, and asks where it comes from. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי עקיבא goes further than the version of בית הלל discussed so far. He allows not only a זר but even a גוי to eat the blemished בכור. The קל וחומר from טמא only reaches a Jewish non-כהן, so a separate source is needed for a גוי.

keyTerms.meaning: The תנא whose report of בית הלל's view is more lenient
Permits
A non-Jew
What is the reason? (a request for a source)

phrases.english: And Rabbi Akiva permits it, and even to a gentile.
phrases.notes: A quote from the ברייתא being analyzed.

phrases.english: What is the reason of Rabbi Akiva?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from בית הלל's derivation for a זר to רבי עקיבא's wider view that includes a גוי.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The scriptural source for allowing a גוי to eat a blemished בכור

steps.title: Like a deer and gazelle: permitted even to a גוי
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק compares a blemished בכור to a צבי and an איל. Just as those may be eaten by a גוי, so may a blemished בכור.
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוק says 'like the gazelle and like the deer.' Just as a gazelle and a deer are permitted to a non-Jew, so too disqualified offerings are permitted to a non-Jew.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question by pointing to the comparison in the פסוק between a blemished בכור and ordinary wild animals.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A צבי and an איל are plain, non-holy animals that anyone, even a גוי, may eat. Since the תורה compares the פסולי המוקדשין to them, רבי עקיבא learns that they too may be given to a גוי. The source is the comparison in the פסוק, not a קל וחומר.

keyTerms.meaning: Like the gazelle and like the deer
Disqualified consecrated animals (here, a blemished בכור)
Permitted

steps.whatToRemember: רבי עקיבא's source for allowing a גוי is the comparison 'כצבי וכאיל.' A blemished בכור is treated like ordinary animals that anyone may eat.

phrases.english: "Like the gazelle and like the deer" —
phrases.notes: דברים 15:22.

phrases.english: just as a gazelle and a deer are permitted to a gentile,
so too disqualified offerings are permitted to a gentile.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 5.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The comparison to a צבי and an איל, which a גוי may eat, shows that a blemished בכור may also be given to a גוי.

steps.title: What does the other opinion do with the verse?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how the תנא who disagrees with רבי עקיבא handles the צבי ואיל comparison.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the other one? (How does he deal with this verse?)
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up its next move. It asks about the other תנא, who does not let a גוי eat a blemished בכור: what does he do with the comparison to צבי ואיל that רבי עקיבא just used?
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי עקיבא learned from the comparison to צבי ואיל that even a גוי may eat a blemished בכור. If the other תנא disagrees, he must explain why this verse does not teach the same thing to him. The answer comes in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: And the other one, meaning the opposing opinion. It asks how that opinion handles the source just quoted.

phrases.english: And the other one (what does he do with this)?
phrases.notes: This refers to the תנא who argues on רבי עקיבא's version of בית הלל.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks how the opposing opinion deals with the derivation brought in Step 6.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: How does the תנא who forbids a גוי to eat a blemished בכור explain the comparison to צבי ואיל?

steps.title: The phrase appears three times, and each one is needed
steps.stepSummary: The words צבי ואיל are written three times, and each appearance is already used for another teaching.
steps.simpleTranslation: The phrase "צבי and איל" is written three times. One is for the teaching of רבי יצחק, one for the teaching of רבי אושעיא, and one for the teaching of רבי אלעזר הקפר.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the comparison to צבי ואיל shows up three separate times in the תורה. Each time, it is already busy teaching something else.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A verse is only used for a new teaching if it is 'extra'. The other תנא says these mentions of צבי ואיל are each already taken by other teachings brought elsewhere. So none of them is free to teach that a גוי may eat a blemished בכור.

keyTerms.meaning: Three
Are written in the תורה
A gazelle and a deer: wild animals that anyone may eat and that are not holy.
One is used for the teaching of a certain רבי

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think the other תנא rejects the comparison to צבי ואיל. He agrees it exists. He just says every appearance of it is already used up, so none is left to teach about a גוי.

phrases.english: "Gazelle and deer" are written three times,
one for the teaching of Rabbi Yitzchak,
and one for the teaching of Rabbi Oshaya,
phrases.notes: The Sefaria translation treats the teachings of רבי יצחק and רבי אושעיא as sharing one appearance. That leaves the 'other one' in the next line for the third appearance.

phrases.english: and one for the teaching of Rabbi Elazar HaKappar.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 7.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Each appearance of צבי ואיל is already used for other teachings, so none is free to teach about a גוי.

steps.title: The last appearance teaches an exemption from בכורה
steps.stepSummary: The remaining appearance teaches that animals from disqualified קדשים are exempt from בכורה, just like a צבי and an איל.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the other one teaches this: just as a צבי and an איל are exempt from the law of the firstborn, so too disqualified holy animals are exempt from the law of the firstborn.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes its list. The last appearance of צבי ואיל teaches that פסולי המוקדשין, holy animals that became disqualified, do not have the law of בכורה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Wild animals like a צבי have no firstborn law, because בכורה applies only to herd and flock animals. The verse compares פסולי המוקדשין to them, so their firstborn is also exempt. With this, all appearances are used up, and the other תנא has no source to allow a גוי to eat a blemished בכור.

keyTerms.meaning: Exempt from the law that the firstborn is holy
Holy animals that became disqualified, usually through a blemish, and were redeemed
Just as... so too: the formula for comparing two cases

steps.whatToRemember: The other תנא does not let a גוי eat a blemished בכור. His reason is that every appearance of צבי ואיל is already used for other teachings, and the last one teaches that פסולי המוקדשין are exempt from בכורה.

phrases.english: And the other (appearance)?
phrases.notes: Here it means 'the remaining verse', not a new challenge.

phrases.aramaic: מָה צְבִי וְאַיָּל פְּטוּרִים מִן הַבְּכוֹרָה,
phrases.english: Just as a gazelle and a deer are exempt from the firstborn law,
so too disqualified consecrated animals
are exempt from the firstborn law.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִידַּךְ? מָה צְבִי וְאַיָּל פְּטוּרִים מִן הַבְּכוֹרָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the list of uses begun in Step 8.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The final appearance teaches that the offspring of פסולי המוקדשין is exempt from בכורה.

steps.title: A dispute about feeding a בכור to נדות
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא records that בית שמאי forbid feeding a בכור to נדות, while בית הלל permit it.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Rabbis taught: a בכור may not be given to נדות to eat. These are the words of בית שמאי. בית הלל say: it may be given to נדות to eat.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new topic with a ברייתא. בית שמאי and בית הלל argue about whether women who are נדות, and so ritually impure, may eat from a blemished בכור.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This continues the theme of who may eat a blemished בכור, now focusing on people who are טמא. בית שמאי forbid it to נדות. Step 14 shows they still let someone with outside impurity eat it. בית הלל allow it even to נדות.

keyTerms.meaning: The Rabbis taught: introduces a ברייתא
We may feed or give to eat
Women who are נדה and therefore ritually impure
A firstborn animal. Here it means one with a blemish.

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught:
A firstborn may not be given to menstruating women to eat,
these are the words of Beit Shammai.
And Beit Hillel say:
It may be given to menstruating women to eat.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new ברייתא on a related question: whether a טמא may eat a blemished בכור.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: בית שמאי: a בכור may not be fed to נדות. בית הלל: it may.

steps.title: What is בית שמאי's reason?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the source of בית שמאי's ruling.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason of בית שמאי?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up its next move. It asks why בית שמאי forbid feeding a blemished בכור to נדות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A blemished בכור may be eaten outside the מקדש, so it seems close to ordinary meat. The גמרא wants to know what makes בית שמאי treat it as holy meat that a טמא may not eat.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the reason?

phrases.english: What is the reason of Beit Shammai?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the source of the first opinion in the ברייתא.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What source tells בית שמאי that נדות may not eat a בכור?

steps.title: The בכור is compared to the חזה ושוק
steps.stepSummary: The verse 'their flesh shall be yours' compares the בכור to the חזה ושוק, which נדות may not eat.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is written: 'And their flesh shall be yours', like the חזה ושוק. Just as there, נדות may not eat, so too here, נדות may not eat.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives בית שמאי's source. The תורה compares the meat of the בכור to the חזה ושוק, the breast and thigh of a שלמים, and those may not be eaten by a טמא person.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The verse links the בכור to the חזה ושוק. Since the חזה ושוק are holy meat that a טמא may not eat, בית שמאי say נדות may not eat a בכור either, even a blemished one. As step 14 shows, they do not extend this ban to someone whose impurity came from an outside source.

keyTerms.meaning: 'And their flesh shall be yours' (במדבר 18:18), said about the בכור
The breast and thigh of a שלמים, given to the כהן and eaten only in טהרה
There / here: the two cases being compared

steps.confusionAlert: The words 'חזה ושוק' do not appear in the גמרא's quote here. They come from the end of the same verse ('like the חזה התנופה וכשוק הימין'), and that is the 'there' being compared to.

phrases.english: As it is written: "And their flesh shall be yours",
phrases.notes: The verse continues: like the wave breast and the right thigh.

phrases.english: just as there, menstruating women may not (eat),
so too here, menstruating women may not (eat).

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 11.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The בכור is compared to the חזה ושוק, which a טמא may not eat.

steps.title: בית הלל: the comparison applies only to an unblemished בכור
steps.stepSummary: בית הלל limit the comparison to an unblemished בכור, because about a blemished one the תורה says the טמא and the טהור may eat it.
steps.simpleTranslation: And בית הלל say: this applies to an unblemished בכור. But about a blemished one, the תורה says: 'the impure and the pure may eat it.'
steps.whatsHappening: בית הלל answer בית שמאי's proof. They say the comparison to the חזה ושוק is only about a תם, an unblemished בכור. For a blemished בכור, the תורה openly allows even a טמא to eat it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: בית הלל accept the verse but narrow its scope to a תם. For a בעל מום, another verse (דברים 15:22) clearly says 'הטמא והטהור', so a נדה may eat it. בית שמאי's proof therefore does not cover the case in the ברייתא.

keyTerms.meaning: These words apply (only to...): used to limit a teaching
Unblemished
Blemished
'The impure and the pure may eat it' (based on דברים 15:22)

steps.whatToRemember: בית שמאי compare every בכור to the חזה ושוק, so no טמא may eat it. בית הלל limit that comparison to a תם. A blemished בכור may be eaten even by a טמא, because the תורה says 'הטמא והטהור'.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows a common pattern in the גמרא. Instead of rejecting the other side's verse, one side limits it to a narrower case and uses a second verse for the other case.

phrases.english: And Beit Hillel (respond):
this applies to an unblemished one,
but a blemished one —
"the impure and the pure may eat it."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers בית שמאי's derivation from Step 12 by limiting it.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Partial: the comparison stays in place for a תם, but it does not apply to a בעל מום.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: בית שמאי applied the comparison to the חזה ושוק to a blemished בכור, but a separate verse permits a blemished בכור to the טמא.

steps.title: בית שמאי limit the verse to outside impurity
steps.stepSummary: בית שמאי answer בית הלל: the verse letting a טמא eat a blemished בכור only covers someone whose impurity came from outside, not someone whose impurity comes from his own body, like a נדה.
steps.simpleTranslation: And בית שמאי would say: That verse applies only where the impurity does not come upon a person from his own body. But where the impurity comes from his own body, it does not apply.
steps.whatsHappening: בית שמאי defend their ruling against בית הלל's challenge. They agree the תורה allows a טמא to eat a blemished בכור, but say this does not include a נדה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: בית הלל had said that a blemished בכור may be eaten by 'the טמא and the טהור', so a נדה should be allowed. בית שמאי narrow the word 'טמא' here. It means someone who became impure from an outside source, such as a dead body or a שרץ. Impurity that comes out of a person's own body, like a נדה or זב, is a stricter type and is not included.

keyTerms.meaning: This statement applies only to... (introduces a limit)
Impurity that comes from one's own body (זב, נדה, יולדת, מצורע)
Where / in a case where

steps.confusionAlert: בית שמאי are not arguing with the verse. They accept that a טמא may eat a blemished בכור. They only limit which kind of טמא the verse means.

phrases.english: And Beit Shammai [would say]:
This statement applies

phrases.aramaic: הֵיכָא דְּאֵין טוּמְאָה יוֹצְאָה עָלָיו מִגּוּפוֹ,
phrases.english: where the impurity does not come upon him from his own body,
phrases.notes: For example, impurity from a corpse or a שרץ.

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל הֵיכָא דְּטוּמְאָה יוֹצְאָה עָלָיו מִגּוּפוֹ
phrases.english: but where the impurity comes upon him from his own body
phrases.notes: For example, a זב or a נדה.

phrases.english: — it does not apply.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּבֵית שַׁמַּאי, הָנֵי מִילֵּי הֵיכָא דְּאֵין טוּמְאָה יוֹצְאָה עָלָיו מִגּוּפוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers בית הלל's challenge from the verse about a blemished בכור by narrowing what 'טמא' in that verse means.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the scope of a verse (distinction between types of impurity)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The verse 'the טמא and the טהור' allows every kind of טמא, including a נדה, to eat a blemished בכור.
steps.terutzMaskana: The verse only includes impurity from an outside source. Impurity from one's own body is excluded, so נדות may not eat a בכור.

steps.title: Proof from a פסח offering brought in impurity
steps.stepSummary: בית שמאי prove the תורה treats bodily impurity more strictly, from the משנה that people with bodily impurity may not eat a פסח brought in טומאה.
steps.simpleTranslation: For we find that the תורה distinguishes between impurity that comes from one's own body and impurity that does not, as we learned in a משנה: when the פסח is brought in a state of impurity, זבים, מצורעים, זבות, נדות and יולדות may not eat from it.
steps.whatsHappening: בית שמאי bring a source to show that their distinction is real and not invented. They point to a משנה about the קרבן פסח.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When most of the people are impure from a dead body, the פסח is brought and eaten in טומאה. Even so, people whose impurity comes from their own body still may not eat it. This shows the תורה itself separates the two types of impurity, so בית שמאי apply the same split to בכור.

keyTerms.meaning: For we have found
The תורה (רחמנא, the Merciful One) distinguishes
A פסח offering brought while most of the people are impure
Men with a זיבה discharge and people with צרעת
Women after childbirth

phrases.english: For we find that the Merciful One distinguishes
between impurity that comes upon him from his own body,

phrases.aramaic: לְבֵין שֶׁאֵין טוּמְאָה יוֹצְאָה עָלָיו מִגּוּפוֹ,
phrases.english: and impurity that does not come upon him from his own body,
as we learned in a mishna: The Paschal offering that is brought in impurity —
phrases.notes: משנה in פסחים צה:

phrases.english: may not be eaten from
by zavim and lepers
and zavot and menstruating women and women after childbirth.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּאַשְׁכְּחַן דְּפַלֵּיג רַחֲמָנָא בֵּין טוּמְאָה יוֹצְאָה עָלָיו מִגּוּפוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports בית שמאי's distinction from step 14 with a source from the laws of פסח.
steps.raayaObject: בית שמאי's claim that bodily impurity is stricter than outside impurity
steps.raayaSupportSource: משנה in פסחים: a פסח brought in טומאה may not be eaten by זבים, מצורעים, זבות, נדות, and יולדות

steps.title: בית הלל: the פסח verse is specific, the בכור verse is general
steps.stepSummary: בית הלל reject the proof: by פסח the תורה specifically wrote 'טמא נפש' (impure from a dead body), but by בכור it wrote just 'טמא', which includes every kind of impurity.
steps.simpleTranslation: And בית הלל would answer: There, by פסח, the תורה revealed 'impure by a dead body.' But here, by בכור, 'impure' is written without limits, so there is no difference.
steps.whatsHappening: בית הלל push back on בית שמאי's proof from פסח. They show why the פסח case cannot be copied over to בכור.
steps.deeperAnalysis: By פסח, the verse spells out 'טמא נפש', so only that kind of impurity is allowed. By בכור, the verse just says 'טמא' with no details. A general word includes all kinds of impurity, so a נדה may eat a blemished בכור.

keyTerms.meaning: The תורה revealed / spelled out
Impure from a dead body (במדבר ט:י)
It is written without details (unspecified)
There is no difference

steps.whatToRemember: בית שמאי: bodily impurity (like a נדה) is stricter, as by פסח, so נדות may not eat a בכור. בית הלל: by פסח the verse is specific ('טמא נפש'), but by בכור it says plain 'טמא', so all impure people, even נדות, may eat a blemished בכור.

phrases.english: And Beit Hillel [would respond]:
It is there that the Merciful One revealed
"Impure by reason of a dead body,"
phrases.notes: במדבר ט:י, about פסח שני.

phrases.english: but here, "impure" is written unspecified,
phrases.notes: דברים טו:כב, about a blemished בכור.

phrases.english: so there is no difference.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּבֵית הִלֵּל: הָתָם הוּא דְּגַלִּי רַחֲמָנָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects בית שמאי's proof from פסח in step 15 by showing the wording of the verses is different.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the comparison from פסח to בכור, not the rule about פסח itself
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The פסח verse specifically limits itself to 'טמא נפש', while the בכור verse says plain 'טמא', so the distinction cannot be carried over.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: According to בית הלל, every kind of טמא, including נדות, may eat a blemished בכור.

steps.title: No skinning from the feet on יום טוב, a בכור, or פסולי המוקדשין
steps.stepSummary: A new ברייתא teaches that one may not skin an animal from its feet (keeping the hide whole) on יום טוב, and likewise not a בכור or פסולי המוקדשין.
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן taught: One may not skin an animal from its feet on יום טוב. Similarly, one may not skin a בכור from its feet, nor פסולי המוקדשין.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new topic with a ברייתא. It lists cases where skinning an animal 'from the feet' (מרגילין) is not allowed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Skinning from the feet keeps the hide whole so it can be used as a container. On יום טוב this is forbidden because it is extra work not needed for food. By a בכור and פסולי המוקדשין it is forbidden even on a weekday, because it treats holy animals with disrespect, even after they were redeemed.

keyTerms.meaning: The Sages taught (introduces a ברייתא)
Skinning an animal starting from its feet, keeping the hide whole
A festival day
Similarly / in the same way
Consecrated animals that became unfit (blemished) and were redeemed

steps.confusionAlert: The reasons are different. On יום טוב the problem is extra unnecessary work. By a בכור and פסולי המוקדשין the problem is disrespect to holy animals, so it applies even on a weekday.

phrases.english: The Sages taught:
One may not skin an animal from its feet on a Festival,
Similarly,
one may not skin a firstborn from its feet,
nor disqualified consecrated animals.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: אֵין מַרְגִּילִין בְּיוֹם טוֹב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic after the בית שמאי / בית הלל debate ends.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One may not skin an animal from its feet on יום טוב, and the same applies to a בכור and to פסולי המוקדשין.

steps.title: Why does the ברייתא forbid this for a בכור?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא accepts the יום טוב reason: it is pointless effort on the festival. It then asks which תנא holds that a בכור may not be skinned from the feet.
steps.simpleTranslation: It makes sense for יום טוב, because he is putting in effort that does not help him on the festival. But for a בכור, who taught this?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the easy part of the ברייתא (יום טוב). Then it asks about the hard part: why a בכור? This sets up רב חסדא's answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Skinning from the feet keeps the hide in one piece, which you would only want for later use, not for the festival. So on יום טוב it is extra work for no festival purpose. A blemished בכור, though, is normally eaten like ordinary meat, so there seems to be no reason to forbid it.

keyTerms.meaning: It makes sense / granted (the גמרא accepts one part before asking about another)
Effort that is of no use to him (on the festival)
Who is the תנא (which sage holds this view)?

phrases.english: Granted, on a festival it is forbidden,

phrases.aramaic: דְּקָא טָרַח טִירְחָא דְּלָא חֲזֵי לֵיהּ.
phrases.english: because he is exerting effort that is of no use to him (for the festival).
phrases.notes: Keeping the hide whole only helps after the festival.

phrases.english: But a firstborn — who is the תנא who taught this?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Analyzes the ברייתא quoted in step 17.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which תנא forbids skinning a בכור from its feet?

steps.title: The בכור ruling follows בית שמאי
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא says this follows בית שמאי, who hold that a בכור may not be fed to נדות. That shows they keep treating even a blemished בכור as holy meat.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חסדא said: It is בית שמאי, who say we may not feed it to women who are נדות.
steps.whatsHappening: רב חסדא answers the question. The ruling about a בכור matches בית שמאי, from the argument we saw earlier.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier, בית שמאי held that a blemished בכור may not be fed to a נדה, because it keeps a level of holiness. Since it is still treated like holy meat, you may not handle it in an ordinary, everyday way, such as skinning it from the feet to save the hide. בית הלל, who let anyone eat it, would not need this restriction.

keyTerms.meaning: The school of שמאי
We may not feed (it to them)
Women who are impure from menstruation

steps.whyThisMatters: This ties the ברייתא back to the long argument between בית שמאי and בית הלל in steps 10–16.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב חִסְדָּא: בֵּית שַׁמַּאי הִיא,
phrases.english: Rav Chisda said: It is the view of Beit Shammai,
who say that we may not feed it to menstruating women.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב חִסְדָּא: בֵּית שַׁמַּאי הִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 18.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The ברייתא follows בית שמאי, who treat a blemished בכור with the strictness of holy meat.

steps.title: Who forbids this for disqualified sacrifices?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא moves to the last part of the ברייתא, about פסולי המוקדשין, and asks which תנא holds it.
steps.simpleTranslation: "And not with disqualified sacrifices." Who taught this?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the next phrase of the ברייתא and asks the same question again. This sets up the next answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: פסולי המוקדשין are sacrificial animals that got a blemish and were redeemed, so they are usually eaten like ordinary meat. So why should skinning them from the feet be forbidden? We need a תנא who holds they still keep some holiness.

keyTerms.meaning: Sacrificial animals that became blemished and were redeemed

phrases.english: "And not with disqualified consecrated animals." Who is the תנא?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Parallel question about the next clause of the ברייתא.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which תנא holds that פסולי המוקדשין may not be skinned from the feet?

steps.title: It follows רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא names רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון as the source and introduces a quoted teaching to prove it.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חסדא said: It is רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון, as we learned:
steps.whatsHappening: רב חסדא gives the answer. Then he says "as we learned," which sets up the source that proves it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב חסדא is claiming that רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון holds that disqualified sacrifices keep their holiness even after they are redeemed and slaughtered. The next steps bring the source that shows this.

keyTerms.meaning: רבי אלעזר, son of רבי שמעון (בר יוחאי)
As we learned (introduces a quoted source)

phrases.english: Rav Chisda said:
It is the view of Rabbi Elazar, son of Rabbi Shimon,
as we learned:

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב חִסְדָּא: רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן הִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 20.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The ruling about פסולי המוקדשין follows רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון.

steps.title: The case of two sin offerings
steps.stepSummary: Someone set aside two חטאות, one unblemished and one blemished. The unblemished one is offered, and the blemished one is redeemed. If the blemished one was slaughtered before the other's blood was sprinkled, it is permitted. If it was slaughtered after, it is forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: He had two sin offerings, one unblemished and one blemished. The unblemished one is offered, and the blemished one is redeemed. If the blemished one was slaughtered before the blood of the unblemished one was sprinkled, it is permitted. If it was slaughtered after the blood of the unblemished one was sprinkled, it is forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: This is the first part of the quoted source, the view of the first תנא. It sets up the case so we can see how רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון disagrees in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A חטאת whose owner already got atonement through a different animal must be left to die and is forbidden. Once the unblemished one's blood is sprinkled, the owner has his atonement. So the timing matters. If the blemished animal was already slaughtered before that moment, the first תנא says it is safe: it became ordinary meat. If it was still alive at that moment, it falls under the forbidden category.

keyTerms.meaning: Sin offerings
Unblemished (animal)
Blemished (animal)
Must be redeemed (its holiness is moved onto money)
Its blood was sprinkled on the altar

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think the blemished animal stops being a חטאת just because it is redeemed. The whole question here is how long some of its holiness stays connected to it.

phrases.english: If there were before him two sin offerings,
one unblemished and one blemished —
the unblemished one is offered, the blemished one is redeemed.
If the blemished one was slaughtered,
phrases.notes: After being redeemed.

phrases.aramaic: אִם עַד שֶׁלֹּא נִזְרַק דָּמָהּ שֶׁל תְּמִימָה — מוּתֶּרֶת,
phrases.english: if this was before the blood of the unblemished one was sprinkled — it is permitted,

phrases.aramaic: אִם מִשֶּׁנִּזְרַק דָּמָהּ שֶׁל תְּמִימָה — אֲסוּרָה.
phrases.english: if it was after the blood of the unblemished one was sprinkled — it is forbidden.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: The quoted source introduced by דתנן in step 21.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Once the blemished חטאת has been slaughtered, sprinkling the other's blood no longer forbids it. Only a blemished animal still alive at that moment becomes forbidden.

steps.title: Even meat in the pot stays holy
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון says that even if the meat is already cooking in the pot, sprinkling the other animal's blood makes it forbidden. This shows that, in his view, disqualified sacrifices keep their holiness.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון says: Even if the meat is in the pot, and then the blood of the unblemished one was sprinkled, it is forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: This is the key line that proves רב חסדא's claim. רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון holds that the blemished חטאת stays holy even after it is slaughtered.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For the first תנא, slaughtering the blemished animal ended its link to holiness. For רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון, even meat sitting in the pot can still become forbidden, so the holiness never fully left. If disqualified sacrifices stay holy like that, you may not treat them in an everyday way, like skinning from the feet. That matches the ברייתא.

keyTerms.meaning: Meat (already cooking) in the pot
Forbidden

steps.whatToRemember: The ברייתא's two rulings are each tied to a specific view. The בכור ruling follows בית שמאי. The פסולי המוקדשין ruling follows רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון, who holds that disqualified sacrifices stay holy even as cooked meat.

phrases.english: Rabbi Elazar, son of Rabbi Shimon, says:
Even if the meat is in the pot,
and the blood of the unblemished one was then sprinkled — it is forbidden.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן אוֹמֵר: אֲפִילּוּ בָּשָׂר בִּקְדֵירָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disagrees with the first תנא in step 22. This disagreement is what proves רב חסדא's claim.
steps.raayaObject: רב חסדא's claim that the פסולי המוקדשין clause follows רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון
steps.raayaSupportSource: His ruling that a blemished חטאת becomes forbidden even when its meat is already cooking, which shows it keeps its holiness after slaughter

steps.title: Why not attribute the whole ברייתא to בית שמאי?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רב חסדא. Since בית שמאי already treat a blemished בכור as holy meat, he could have used בית שמאי for the entire ברייתא, without bringing in a second תנא.
steps.simpleTranslation: But רב חסדא should explain the whole ברייתא according to בית שמאי!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why רב חסדא used two different תנאים for one ברייתא. One authority, בית שמאי, seems to be enough.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 19, רב חסדא used בית שמאי for the first part of the ברייתא. In steps 21–23, he used רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון for the last part. The challenge is that בית שמאי, who hold that holiness stays even after a blemish, should also fit the last part, so the split looks unnecessary.

keyTerms.meaning: Let him set it up, meaning explain the text as following a certain view
All of it, meaning the entire ברייתא
The school of שמאי, which is often stricter than בית הלל

phrases.english: And Rav Ḥisda,
phrases.notes: The challenge is aimed directly at רב חסדא's approach.

phrases.english: let him establish all of it according to Beit Shammai!
phrases.notes: Why split the ברייתא between two different תנאים?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַב חִסְדָּא, לוֹקְמַהּ כּוּלַּהּ כְּבֵית שַׁמַּאי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions why רב חסדא needed רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון for the last part of the ברייתא.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב חסדא's choice to attribute the ברייתא to two different תנאים.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: One תנא, בית שמאי, seems to explain both parts. Splitting the ברייתא between two authorities is therefore unnecessary.

steps.title: A בכור's holiness starts at birth, unlike other sacrifices
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that בית שמאי may be strict only about a בכור, because its holiness comes from the womb. Other disqualified sacrifices became holy only when a person set them aside, so בית שמאי might not keep their holiness after slaughter.
steps.simpleTranslation: Perhaps בית שמאי only said their ruling about a בכור, whose holiness is from the womb. But about פסולי המוקדשין, whose holiness is not from the womb, they would not say it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends רב חסדא. It explains that בית שמאי's strict view might only apply to a בכור, so a second תנא is needed for the last part of the ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A בכור is holy automatically from the moment it is born. No person makes it holy. Regular sacrifices become holy only when someone dedicates them, so their holiness may be weaker once a blemish disqualifies them. Because of that possible difference, רב חסדא needed רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון, who clearly holds that even regular disqualified sacrifices stay holy.

keyTerms.meaning: Perhaps
They only said their ruling up to here, meaning in this case alone
Its holiness comes from the womb, meaning it is holy from birth
Sacrifices that were dedicated and then disqualified, usually by a blemish

steps.whatToRemember: A בכור is holy from birth, so its holiness may be stronger than that of a sacrifice a person dedicated. That is why רב חסדא needs רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון for פסולי המוקדשין, and cannot rely on בית שמאי alone.
steps.confusionAlert: The גמרא says "דִּלְמָא" (perhaps). It does not prove that בית שמאי are lenient about פסולי המוקדשין. It only shows that we cannot be sure they are strict, and that uncertainty is enough to justify using another תנא.

phrases.english: Perhaps they only said it until here
phrases.notes: This limits how far בית שמאי's ruling reaches.

phrases.english: Beit Shammai, only regarding a firstborn,
whose sanctity is from the womb,
phrases.notes: It is holy automatically from birth.

phrases.english: but disqualified consecrated animals,
whose sanctity is not from the womb — no.
phrases.notes: Their holiness came from a person dedicating them, so it may be weaker.

steps.triggerLanguage: דִּלְמָא עַד כָּאן לָא קָאָמְרִי בֵּית שַׁמַּאי אֶלָּא בִּבְכוֹר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 24 by drawing a distinction between a בכור and other sacrifices.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinction (חילוק) between kinds of holiness: holiness from birth versus holiness from dedication.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: בית שמאי's strictness about a blemished בכור applies equally to all disqualified sacrifices, so one תנא covers the whole ברייתא.
steps.terutzMaskana: בית שמאי may be strict only about a בכור, whose holiness is from the womb. Therefore רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון is needed for the last part of the ברייתא.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows a key idea: holiness that comes on its own from birth may be stronger and longer-lasting than holiness a person creates by dedicating an animal.
